question.prompt: Elmer the emu takes \(44\) equal strides to walk between consecutive telephone poles on a rural road. Oscar the ostrich can cover the same distance in \(12\) equal leaps. The telephone poles are evenly spaced, and the \(41\)st pole along this road is exactly one mile (\(5280\) feet) from the first pole. How much longer, in feet, is Oscar’s leap than Elmer’s stride?

solutions.title: Count the gaps between poles
solutions.explanation:
From the first pole to the \(41\)st pole, there are \(41-1=40\) equal gaps. Thus consecutive poles are
\[
\frac{5280}{40}=132\text{ feet apart}.
\]
Elmer covers this distance in \(44\) strides, so each stride measures \(132/44=3\) feet. Oscar covers it in \(12\) leaps, so each leap measures \(132/12=11\) feet.

Oscar’s leap is therefore \(11-3=\boxed{8}\) feet longer, choice \(\text{B}\).
